newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA CALLS ON ISRAEL TO 'MANIFEST GOODWILL'.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA CALLS ON ISRAEL TO 'MANIFEST GOODWILL'.

text.p: South Africa on Thursday expressed its deep concern over bloody clashes in the Middle East and urged Israel to show goodwill by honouring its commitments to the peace process.

The Department of Foreign Affairs in Pretoria said it had called in the Israeli and Palestinian ambassadors to express its "deep concerns" over renewed violence on the West Bank and Gaza Strip and urged both sides to return to dialogue.
"These tragic events underline the urgency and necessity of resuming the momentum of the Middle East peace process, already stalled for many months," it said in a statement.

"(South Africa) calls on all parties to restart a meaningful dialogue towards peace, and appeals to Israel to manifest goodwill by honouring its commitments under the Oslo Accords at the earliest possible opportunity."
Norway played a lead role in brokering secret negotiations that led to the signing in Oslo of the historic peace pact between Israel and the Palestinian Liberation Organisation in 1993.

At least 33 Palestinians and 10 Israelis have died in two days of running battles after Israel opened a controversial archaeological tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem near Islam's third-holiest shrine on Tuesday.

President Nelson Mandela, who led South Africa's transition from apartheid to democracy, ending in all-race elections in 1994, is to pay his first visit to the Middle East in November with a tour that includes Israel and Palestinian territories.
Mandela's ruling African National Congress (ANC) for decades identified with the PLO, Israel's former arch-foe, while the ANC struggled against white-led South African rule.
Israel officially opposed apartheid. But facing world criticism over its treatment of Palestinians, Israel shared a sense of isolation with South Africa.
Since then, relations have thawed and South Africa's Foreign Minister, Alfred Nzo, declared a desire to forge strong ties when he visited Israel last September.
